# Test fixtures

Committed KDBX vaults used by the integration and protocol-conformance suites.
Generated by `src/bin/gen_fixtures.rs`; regenerate with:

```sh
cargo run --features cli --bin gen-fixtures
```

Every fixture is encrypted with the password `test-password-do-not-use` (the same
throwaway password `web-kdbx` and `diff-kdbx` use). These are not secrets and must
never hold a real one.

The tests assert against the contents described below. If you change a fixture,
update this manifest and the assertions that read it. The generator does not
produce byte-stable output (keepass assigns random UUIDs and KDBX4 uses a fresh
nonce per save), so UUIDs are not documented here; tests resolve entries by path
and title, not by UUID.

## `empty.kdbx`

A valid vault with no entries and no subgroups (root group only). Exercises the
zero-entry list shapes and an unlock that has nothing to read.

## `flat.kdbx`

Five entries directly under the root group:

| Title  | UserName            | URL                        | Password (protected) | Custom fields                |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------------|----------------------|------------------------------|
| GitHub | octocat             | https://github.com         | `gh-secret-123`      | (Notes: "primary dev account") |
| Bank   | alice               | https://bank.example.com   | `bank-secret-456`    | `PIN` = `4321` (protected)   |
| Email  | alice@example.com   | https://mail.example.com   | `email-secret-789`   |                              |
| Server | root                | ssh://server.example.com   | `server-secret-abc`  | `Port` = `22` (unprotected)  |
| Wifi   |                     |                            | `wifi-secret-def`    |                              |

Covers: standard fields, an implicitly protected password, a custom protected
field (`Bank.PIN`, the reveal-protected happy path), a custom unprotected field
(`Server.Port`, the FIELD_NOT_PROTECTED path), and an entry with neither username
nor url (`Wifi`).

## `nested.kdbx`

Three levels of group nesting under the root: `Personal / Finance / Banking`, with
one entry in the deepest group:

- `/Personal/Finance/Banking/Checking Account` (UserName `alice`, URL
  `https://bank.example.com`, protected Password `checking-secret-xyz`).

Covers group-path resolution at depth.

## `with_attachments.kdbx`

Two entries in the root, each with one binary attachment:

| Entry      | UserName | Attachment   | Content                         |
|------------|----------|--------------|---------------------------------|
| Document A | alice    | `notes.txt`  | `meeting notes\n` (14 bytes)    |
| Document B | bob      | `data.bin`   | the 256 bytes `0x00..=0xff`     |

Covers `kdbx_list_attachments`, `kdbx_download_attachment`, and the base64
round-trip of binary content.

## `with_otp.kdbx`

One entry, `TOTP Account` (UserName `alice`), whose `otp` field holds an otpauth
URI with the canonical RFC 6238 test secret `JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP` (period 30, 6
digits, SHA1). A code can always be produced, for the `kdbx_get_otp` happy path.

## `duplicates.kdbx`

Two entries in the root, both titled `Duplicate`, distinguished only by username
(`first-account`, `second-account`). The path resolver must address them by the
`:1` / `:2` ordinal suffix.

## `kdbx41.kdbx`

One entry, `Note` (UserName `carol`, protected Password `kdbx41-secret-ghi`), in
a file whose header says KDBX 4.1 (written by keepass 0.12 with its config
version set to 4.1, so it holds no 4.1-only data). keepass 0.12 would save a
4.1 file lossily, so the server opens it read-only: reads and reveals work, and
the write tools return `FORMAT_READ_ONLY`. Covers the save-support gate.
